roots.title: Nonlinear Programming
roots.top_down_role: Adaptive-depth structural navigation for Nonlinear Programming; formal statements are stored in a later sidecar layer.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonlinear program in standard equality-and-inequality form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\ge 1\), let \(E\) and \(I\) be disjoint finite index sets, and let \(f,c_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) for every \(i\in E\cup I\). A nonlinear program is an optimization problem
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_i(x)=0\ \text{for all }i\in E,\qquad c_i(x)\ge 0\ \text{for all }i\in I,
\]
in which at least one of the functions \(f\) or \(c_i\), with \(i\in E\cup I\), is not affine. Its feasible set is
\[
F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:c_i(x)=0\ \text{for all }i\in E,\ c_i(x)\ge 0\ \text{for all }i\in I\}.
\]
A point \(x^*\in F\) is a global minimizer if \(f(x^*)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). It is a local minimizer if there exists \(\delta>0\) such that \(f(x^*)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\) satisfying \(\lVert x-x^*\rVert_2<\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional nonlinear program minimizes a real-valued objective subject to finitely many equality and inequality constraints, with at least one objective or constraint function nonaffine. A feasible point is a global minimizer if its objective value is no greater than that of every feasible point, and it is a local minimizer if this comparison holds for all feasible points within some positive Euclidean distance.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(I\) are disjoint finite index sets.
At least one of \(f\) or \(c_i\), with \(i\in E\cup I\), is not affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set is \(F\); global minimizers compare against every point in \(F\), while local minimizers compare against every point of \(F\) in some positive-radius Euclidean neighborhood.

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the nonlinear program.
A feasible point being classified as a local or global minimizer.
Positive radius in the definition of a local minimizer.

children.title: Line Search and Descent Globalization
children.top_down_role: Globalization of smooth unconstrained descent methods through step-length selection, together with nonlinear conjugate-gradient methods whose behavior is governed by line-search acceptance. Trust-region, constrained merit-function, filter, and model-construction theories are referenced but not developed here.

children.title: Trust-Region Methods and Model Adequacy
children.top_down_role: Trust-region globalization, local-model fidelity, trust-region subproblem geometry and solvers, convergence and complexity families, and characteristic failure boundaries.

children.title: Newton Methods and Linear Solvers
children.top_down_role: Newton systems for nonlinear equations, smooth optimization, equality-constrained models, inexact linear solves, matrix-free realizations, subspace reductions, and the Newton-system interfaces of SQP and constrained globalization.

children.title: Quasi-Newton and Variable-Metric Methods
children.top_down_role: Matrix-update models for smooth unconstrained optimization, their structural derivations, computational realizations, convergence families, and characteristic failure boundaries.

children.title: Nonlinear Equations and Least-Squares Methods
children.top_down_role: Finite-dimensional numerical methods and theory for smooth residual systems, nonlinear root finding, and structured least-squares objectives; general unconstrained optimization, linear least squares, complementarity, and polynomial-system algebra are linked but not developed here.

children.title: Optimality and Active-Set Theory for Constrained NLP
children.top_down_role: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear-programming optimality, constraint regularity, second-order geometry, classical sensitivity, active-set identification, and working-set interfaces. Full duality, quadratic-programming solvers, SQP globalization, interior-point methods, and variational-analysis foundations remain in their owning chapters.

children.title: Equality-Constrained Reduction Methods
children.top_down_role: Equality-constrained smooth optimization viewed through tangent-space geometry, elimination, KKT linear algebra, reduced-space algorithms, feasibility management, and their computational boundaries.

children.title: Sequential Quadratic Programming
children.top_down_role: Local and global SQP theory, quadratic models, step computation, globalization, safeguards, convergence regimes, and scalable implementations for smooth nonlinear programming.

children.title: Feasibility Globalization Methods
children.top_down_role: Globalization and feasibility-management structures based on penalization, scalar merit models, filters, restoration, elastic relaxations, and funnels; multiplier algorithms, SQP, trust-region methods, and interior-point methods remain external method chapters.

children.title: Smooth Nonconvex Criticality and Landscape Theory
children.top_down_role: Local and approximate stationarity for smooth nonconvex objectives, the geometry and dynamics of saddle points, and method families for detecting or escaping nonminimizing stationary regions. General constrained optimality theory and full globalization frameworks remain in their owning chapters.

children.title: Smooth Nonconvex Regularization and Complexity
children.top_down_role: Navigation for smooth nonconvex evaluation complexity, trust-region complexity, cubic and arbitrary-order regularization, higher-order criticality, scalable realizations, and sharpness or failure regimes.

children.title: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Convergence and Landscape Analysis
children.top_down_role: Navigation for analytic convergence geometry and smooth nonconvex landscape models, with domain-specific optimization problems retained only through their landscape roles.

children.title: Interior-Point and Barrier Methods
children.top_down_role: Barrier geometry, central-path theory, primal-dual mechanisms, nonlinear-programming algorithms, implementation systems, model interfaces, guarantees, and failure boundaries.

children.title: Augmented Lagrangian Methods
children.top_down_role: Augmented-Lagrangian models, multiplier methods, convergence and complexity theory, subproblem architectures, stabilized variants, and their computational boundaries.
